Worth trying first: willing to maintain fine hand work and concentration for long periods, able to accept repeated verification and infection control procedures, willing to follow standards and guidelines rather than skipping steps based on experience, interested in image interpretation, anatomy and materials, able to communicate with anxious or pained patients, and able to record complications and follow-up results faithfully.

Needs caution: if it is hard to hold the same posture and steady hands for long periods, if one is sensitive to the smell of blood, saliva and disinfectants, if one is unwilling to verify and write records repeatedly, if one prefers quick results and does not accept rechecks and follow-up, or if one is unwilling to ask a supervising physician for help when beyond one's own ability and registration scope, the actual work will not match expectations.

Low-risk verification: do a fictitious record check for the entry case D-02, list two blank fields, and check identity and three status conflicts, review against the reference answers and compile the four portfolio pieces; no real patient information is used, and no diagnosis or procedure is performed.

Decision center: whether one can turn the chief complaint and examination findings, the treatment plan, procedures and infection control, and follow-up into traceable care results for which one is accountable to the patient.

The work is mainly in a dental surgery, mostly in a controlled indoor environment, with long periods of sitting combined with standing to operate, facing patients' mouths at close range and contact with body fluids such as blood and saliva, aerosols, disinfectants and dental radiation; it requires steady fine hand work and chairside rhythm; units differ clearly (individual practices, chain organizations, dental departments of general hospitals, public dental specialty hospitals, teaching hospitals) in professional division of labor, scheduling, billing model and quality management system, and the income structure also differs between independent and employed practice.

Similar adjacent job titles do not mean the same authority: distinguish the dental assistant's chairside assistance and instrument handling, the dental hygienist's licensed examination and scaling, specialty dentists such as orthodontists, oral and maxillofacial surgeons and prosthodontists, the dental laboratory technician's prescription-based fabrication of restorations, and optometry occupations such as opticians; whether one can diagnose independently, prescribe, perform surgery or sign informed consent depends on the jurisdictional licence, registration scope and unit authorization.

Inputs that must be verified: chief complaint and history (including systemic disease, medication and allergy history), intraoral and imaging findings, treatment plans and alternatives, informed consent, infection control and radiation protection requirements, instrument and material information, and medical and follow-up records. What must not be done: do not provide care without practice qualification or beyond registration scope, do not operate on experience when diagnostic evidence is insufficient, do not omit informed consent and medical records, and do not omit instrument sterilization and personal protection procedures.

Fit judgments should combine clinical mentoring observation, case review and patient follow-up feedback, and are not replaced by an interest type or a single test; manual dexterity, spatial and image interpretation ability, and the willingness to bear the pressure of treatment risk and complications must be confirmed in real training and feedback.

All paper exercises on this page use fictitious materials; real patient examination and procedures, anesthesia and prescribing, radiological examination and surgery, and medical record and privacy handling are carried out by licensed and registered physicians under the applicable jurisdictional regulations (such as mainland China's Physicians Law and the practice requirements for the dental category, and U.S. state licence requirements) and unit policies.

The work objects of general dentists are the patients who come for care together with their chief complaints, medical history and intraoral and imaging findings; the outputs are diagnostic conclusions, treatment plans and informed consent, procedure records and medical records, follow-up and referral arrangements, and the prescriptions and specifications sent to the laboratory for restoration fabrication; the basis for treatment is dental medicine guidelines and standards, infection control and radiation protection requirements, drug and material instructions, and the unit's clinical policies, not the occupational title.

Check one: whether the chief complaint and history are complete — whether systemic disease, medication history, allergy history and previous oral treatment are all asked about; missing items must be pursued or handled through the unit's specified process, without drawing conclusions from impressions.

Check two: whether examination and imaging support the diagnosis — whether clinical examination, pulpal and periodontal examination and imaging findings are consistent with each other; when evidence is insufficient, add examinations or recommend referral, and do not begin irreversible procedures on insufficient evidence.

Check three: whether the treatment plan and alternatives are clearly explained and consent obtained — whether indications, risks, prognosis, costs and alternatives are explained to the patient and informed consent recorded.

Check four: whether the procedures are within registration scope and one's own ability — whether anesthesia, medication, surgery and complex procedures fall within one's own practice scope and trained ability; when beyond it, refer or involve a supervising physician according to the process.

Check five: whether infection control and radiation protection are in place — whether instrument sterilization, single-use items, personal protection and imaging protection are carried out according to standards, and whether medical waste is segregated and disposed of as required.

Check six: whether records, follow-up and reporting are traceable — whether medical records, imaging, medication and procedure records are complete, whether complications and recall arrangements are implemented, and whether errors and adverse events are reported as required rather than concealed.

Where are the boundaries between general dentists and the adjacent dental hygienists, dental assistants, orthodontists, oral and maxillofacial surgeons and dental laboratory technicians?

This table compares general dentists with adjacent occupations item by item across seven dimensions: core purpose, main objects and basis, core process, main outputs, responsible party, collaboration and supervision, and conclusion boundaries: these positions are all on the oral and related medical work chain, but the objects (diagnosis and treatment of oral disease, licensed examination and scaling, chairside assistance, correction of malocclusion, oral and maxillofacial surgery, and prescription-based restoration fabrication) and the final clinical responsibility do not shift just because the positions are adjacent. The U.S. occupational code on this page is 29-1021.00 (Dentists, General), which together with orthodontists (29-1023.00), oral and maxillofacial surgeons (29-1022.00) and prosthodontists (29-1024.00) belongs to the official Dentists broad group; when comparing, verify the actual scope of care, workplace and signing or release responsibility item by item.
Core purpose

Examine, diagnose and treat diseases and malformations of the teeth, gums and related oral structures, develop and implement treatment plans, and take responsibility for clinical outcomes and patient safety.

Core purposes of adjacent positions: dental hygienists perform oral examination, scaling and preventive procedures under their licence; dental assistants provide chairside assistance and instrument handling under a dentist's direction; orthodontists diagnose and correct malocclusion; oral and maxillofacial surgeons perform surgery of the oral and maxillofacial region; dental laboratory technicians fabricate restorations in the laboratory according to prescriptions; optometrists handle visual examination and prescribing.
Main objects and basis

The objects are the patient's symptoms and history, intraoral and imaging findings, and the endodontic and periodontal problems requiring treatment; the basis is dental medicine guidelines and standards, infection control and radiation protection requirements, drug and material instructions, and the unit's clinical policies.

Objects and basis of adjacent positions: dental hygienists focus on periodontal and gingival conditions (oral prevention and periodontal care standards and state licensure); dental assistants focus on the patient's mouth and the treatment process (clinical standards and infection control requirements); orthodontists focus on dentofacial malocclusion and growth (orthodontic standards); oral and maxillofacial surgeons focus on maxillofacial disease and trauma (surgical standards and surgical authorization); dental laboratory technicians focus on work orders and impression or scan data (prosthetics process requirements and quality standards); optometrists focus on visual function and refractive status (optometry standards and state licensure).
Core process

Consultation and examination → imaging and pulpal and periodontal assessment → diagnosis and treatment plan → informed consent → performing procedures under anesthesia and isolation → records and prescriptions → recall, education and referral.

Processes of adjacent positions: examination, scaling and preventive procedures (dental hygienists); chairside assistance and instrument handling (dental assistants); impression taking and image analysis, appliance design and recall adjustment (orthodontists); preoperative assessment and surgical procedures (oral and maxillofacial surgeons); prescription-based fabrication and inspection of restorations (dental laboratory technicians); refraction and prescribing (optometrists).
Main outputs
Diagnostic conclusions and medical records, treatment plans and informed consent, completed procedure and medication records, restoration prescriptions, and recall and referral arrangements.

Outputs of adjacent positions: periodontal examination and scaling records (dental hygienists); treatment assistance and instrument sterilization records (dental assistants); treatment plans and stage-by-stage recall records (orthodontists); surgical records and postoperative follow-up (oral and maxillofacial surgeons); restorations and inspection records (dental laboratory technicians); refraction reports and prescriptions (optometrists).
Responsible party

The personnel in this occupation are responsible for the medical judgment behind the diagnosis and treatment plan, the quality of procedures, informed consent and medical records; prescriptions, surgery and final clinical decisions are made by licensed physicians with the corresponding qualifications, and complex or high-risk cases must be referred or discussed according to the process.

Responsible parties of adjacent positions: dental hygienists are responsible for the quality of examination and scaling within their licence; dental assistants are responsible for chairside assistance and instrument handling; orthodontists, oral and maxillofacial surgeons and prosthodontists are each responsible for clinical decisions within their specialty; dental laboratory technicians are responsible for the quality of restorations fabricated to prescription; optometrists are responsible for refraction and prescribing.
Collaboration and supervision

Collaborate with dental hygienists, dental assistants, the laboratory, specialty dentists and nursing staff within the same care process; when cases exceed one's ability or registration scope, or there are infection control hazards or material and equipment anomalies, pause the procedure, review the records and report or refer according to unit policy.

Collaboration of adjacent positions: dental hygienists collaborate with dentists and patients; dental assistants collaborate with dentists and the front desk; orthodontists, oral and maxillofacial surgeons and prosthodontists collaborate with each other and with the laboratory; dental laboratory technicians collaborate with dentists and quality management staff; optometrists collaborate with ophthalmologists and the eyewear dispensing link.
Conclusion boundaries

Similar job titles do not mean the same duties: whether the object is the diagnosis and treatment of oral disease, licensed examination and scaling, chairside assistance, correction of malocclusion, maxillofacial surgery or restoration fabrication, and whether one has the authority to diagnose independently, prescribe, perform surgery and sign informed consent, determines the scope of duties and responsibility and cannot be swapped by title.

The licence scope, preparation levels and regulatory requirements of adjacent and specialty positions do not apply to this occupation and must be verified item by item against each occupation's official materials, the target jurisdiction's regulations and the employing unit's policies; specialty dentists within the same broad group also have different scopes of practice.

Dentists, General (O*NET-SOC 29-1021.00) are licensed physicians responsible for the diagnosis and treatment of oral disease: they assess teeth, gums and related structures through consultation, intraoral examination and imaging, develop treatment plans and obtain informed consent, perform anesthesia, fillings and restorations, root canal treatment, extractions and periodontal treatment and similar procedures under protection and isolation, prescribe medication and commission the laboratory to fabricate restorations when necessary, and also carry out preventive education, recalls and follow-up and practice management; in the United States a state licence is required, and in mainland China the dental category physician qualification examination must be passed and practice registration completed.

Practice management and teaching: arranging staff, procurement and record processes and managing institutional quality records; carrying out teaching, continuing study or research. Specific management posts, teaching qualifications and responsibilities are verified against the unit.

In the United States, dental hygienists examine and scale, provide preventive education and keep records according to state authority; dental assistants prepare patients, instruments and materials and assist with procedures, sterilization and documentation under a dentist's direction. Their respective authority is not equivalent to being an independent dentist.

Orthodontists diagnose malocclusion and design, implement and adjust treatment; oral and maxillofacial surgeons assess and surgically manage oral and maxillofacial disease, trauma and so on, retaining surgical and follow-up records. The two are separate U.S. specialty codes.

Dental laboratory technicians fabricate, repair and inspect restorations to prescription and keep quality records; U.S. optometrists (29-1041.00) examine the visual system, manage vision and eye care problems and prescribe corrective lenses, with drug authority depending on state law.
Direction one within the occupation: comprehensive general practice (examination, fillings and restorations, root canal, extractions, prevention and education)

Form a diagnosis through consultation and intraoral and imaging examination, perform anesthesia, fillings and restorations, root canal treatment, simple extractions and preventive procedures, educate patients and arrange recalls.

Compared with the specialty direction, it covers a broader range of conditions but with less depth in any single condition, and requires independently completing diagnosis and treatment of common conditions and being accountable for the outcome; compared with adjacent occupations, this direction includes the authority to diagnose, prescribe and perform invasive procedures.

If you want to see patients independently as early as possible and are willing to take on the diagnostic judgment and communication for common conditions, you can start in the comprehensive general practice direction.
Direction two within the occupation: specialized care (endodontics, periodontics, prosthodontics, implants, paediatric dentistry and so on)

After completing the corresponding specialty training, concentrate on complex root canal treatment, periodontal surgery, fixed and removable prosthodontics, implant placement and restoration, or paediatric behaviour management and similar areas to handle difficult cases.

Compared with the general practice direction, the training period is longer and case complexity higher, usually requiring a referral network and cooperation; compared with independent specialties such as oral and maxillofacial surgery, the occupational code on this page is still a general dentist subcategory, and specialty scope and authorization follow the jurisdiction and certification.
If you are willing to invest in longer training and prefer handling difficult cases, you can set the specialized direction as a medium- to long-term goal.
Direction three within the occupation: practice management, teaching and quality management

Compared with the other directions, the output shifts from individual cases to replicable processes, teams and quality records, with responsibility covering institutional compliance, personnel management and continuous quality improvement, requiring documentation and management skills.
If you are good at turning clinical experience into written procedures, mentoring others and getting them to follow through, you can move toward practice management, teaching or quality management.
Adjacent occupations: dental hygienists (29-1292.00) and dental assistants (31-9091.00)

Dental hygienists perform oral examination, scaling and preventive procedures under a state licence; dental assistants prepare and sterilize instruments, prepare patients, and assist and record during treatment under a dentist's direction; both work directly with patients' mouths but do not make diagnoses independently, whereas this occupation carries responsibility for diagnosis, treatment plans and invasive procedures, and the transferable common points are infection control, chairside collaboration and medical record standards.

If you would rather interact with patients directly without taking on diagnostic responsibility for now, compare these two directions; if independent diagnosis and treatment is the goal, you need to follow the dental professional education and practice registration path.
Adjacent occupations: orthodontists (29-1023.00) and oral and maxillofacial surgeons (29-1022.00)

Orthodontists specialise in the diagnosis and correction of malocclusion, and oral and maxillofacial surgeons specialise in the surgical treatment of maxillofacial disease and trauma; both have independent codes in O*NET-SOC and longer specialty training; this occupation usually handles the diagnosis and treatment of common oral disease and refers to them when needed, and the common points are the foundations of oral anatomy, image interpretation and infection control.
If you clearly want to do malocclusion correction or maxillofacial surgery, plan the education and training path for that specialty directly rather than waiting on the general dentist path.
Adjacent occupations: dental laboratory technicians (51-9081.00) and optometrists (29-1041.00)

Dental laboratory technicians fabricate, repair and inspect restorations to prescription and specification, and cannot provide independent care on the basis of a technician qualification; U.S. optometrists (29-1041.00) examine the visual system, diagnose and treat vision and eye care problems and prescribe corrective lenses, with specific drug authority following state law. Their service recipients and qualifications differ from those of dentists.

If you prefer independent processing and inspection and do not want clinical responsibility, you can compare the laboratory direction; if you are more interested in optometry, you can look into the optometrist path.

It can assist in generating imaging prompts, record summaries or draft patient education materials, but these must be checked item by item against the clinical examination, the original images and the standards before being used for care or disclosure.

china_edu_table.岗位方向: Physicians Law article 9: a relevant medical bachelor's degree or above plus 1 year of supervised medical practice at a medical institution, or a relevant medical junior college degree plus 2 years of practice after obtaining an assistant practice certificate; the assistant route in article 10 is verified separately, and the article 64 secondary-school transition does not mean all secondary-school graduates may apply. Applicants must meet the appropriate dental specialty or historical enrolment and graduation conditions and pass the examination, and under article 14 practice after registration according to the location and category scope; a physician qualification certificate is not practice registration or institutional filing. Registration takes a statutory 20 working days and is not the whole examination and processing cycle; under article 24 medical documents are issued after personal examination and must not be concealed, forged, altered or destroyed without authorization, while article 25 separates general condition measures from the explanation and explicit consent for surgery and special examinations or treatments with risks and alternatives. The 2014 original text lists historical branches for five-year dental bachelor's degrees and postgraduate or junior college pathways, and qualifications in medical technology or nursing are not a basis for applying. The original Fujian display page is marked as no longer effective, yet the existing NMEC FAQ/2026 Huainan announcement still cites that version, so a single page cannot be used to declare nationwide repeal or to claim that all sections are currently effective; individuals verify the specialty, practice certification and first registration records against the target test centre for the year. The 2026 Huainan notice specifies an interval of 24 months from assistant registration to the comprehensive medical examination for the junior college pathway and 60 months for the historical secondary-school pathway; these are local requirements for that year, not all national conditions.
Consists of the practical skills examination and the comprehensive medical examination; after obtaining qualification, practice registration must be applied for before practising.

The official 2022 clinic measures were actually read: an individual establishing a practice must have 5 years of practice at a medical institution after registration, county-level filing and a certificate and public disclosure of filed subjects and personnel; the five years is a condition for individuals establishing a practice, not an entry requirement for all employed physicians, and institutional filing is not individual registration or radiation licensing, with time limits counted in working days and not treated as the whole processing schedule.

description.text: Dentists, General (O*NET-SOC 29-1021.00) assess teeth, gums and related oral structures through consultation and history taking and intraoral and imaging examination, form a diagnosis and develop a treatment plan, perform anesthesia, fillings and restorations, root canal treatment, extractions and periodontal treatment and similar procedures under protection and isolation, prescribe medication and commission the laboratory to fabricate restorations when necessary, and also carry out oral health education, recalls and follow-up and practice management; the work environment is a controlled indoor dental surgery with long periods of sitting and close-range work, contact with body fluids such as blood and saliva, aerosols, disinfectants and dental radiation, and the wearing of protective equipment. U.S. basis: in this occupation's May 2025 wage data the median annual wage is 170,950 USD (median hourly wage 82.19 USD) and the annual percentiles are 86,250／125,710／170,950／224,040／319,630 USD; the BLS Occupational Outlook publishes about 161,400 positions for the Dentists broad group in 2025 (with the general dentist subcategory about 141,900), a projected increase of 6% in 2025—2035 (employment change about +9,000) and about 4,800 openings per year on average including replacement needs; a licence in the relevant state is required. Mainland China: this is based on the physician qualification examination and practice registration system established by the Physicians Law, and a licensed physician in the dental category must pass the practical skills and comprehensive medical examinations and complete registration; an individual establishing a dental practice must have five years of practice and file under the Interim Measures for the Administration of Clinic Filing; the National Bureau of Statistics 2025 wage release in this round did not provide a figure listed separately for this occupation, and this page visibly marks the gap in the relevant places rather than filling it with an industry average.

subject.name: Dentists, General
subject.summary: Dentists, General (O*NET-SOC 29-1021.00) are licensed physicians responsible for the diagnosis and treatment of oral disease: they assess teeth, gums and related oral structures through consultation, history taking and intraoral and imaging examination, form a diagnosis and develop a treatment plan, perform anesthesia, fillings and restorations, root canal treatment, extractions and periodontal treatment and similar procedures under protection and isolation, prescribe medication and commission the laboratory to fabricate restorations when necessary, and also carry out oral health education, recalls and follow-up and practice management; the outputs are diagnostic conclusions, treatment plans and informed consent, procedure and medication records, medical records and follow-up arrangements, and restoration prescriptions sent to the laboratory for execution. U.S. basis: in this occupation's May 2025 wage data the median annual wage is 170,950 USD (median hourly wage 82.19 USD) and the annual percentiles are 86,250／125,710／170,950／224,040／319,630 USD; the BLS Occupational Outlook publishes about 161,400 positions for the Dentists broad group in 2025 (of which the general dentist subcategory is about 141,900), a projected increase of 6% in 2025—2035 and about 4,800 openings per year on average including replacement needs; a licence in the relevant state is required. Mainland China basis: this is based on the physician qualification examination and practice registration system established by the Physicians Law, and the licensed physician examination may be taken through a relevant medical bachelor's degree plus one year of practice, or a relevant medical junior college degree plus the assistant licensed physician practice certificate and two years of practice; the dental category and historical transitions require verification of the registration rules, and the practical skills and comprehensive medical examinations must be passed and registration completed; an individual establishing a dental practice must have five years of practice after registration and file under the Interim Measures for the Administration of Clinic Filing; the National Bureau of Statistics 2025 wage release in this round did not provide a figure listed separately for this occupation, and this page retains the gap as it stands.
